findings.title: Missing Anti-clickjacking Header
findings.description: The response does not protect against 'ClickJacking' attacks. It should include either Content-Security-Policy with 'frame-ancestors' directive or X-Frame-Options.

verification.evaluation_notes: Endpoint unreachable during verification probe (Probe error: <urlopen error [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it>); remains NEEDS_VERIFICATION.

ai_advisory.gemma_explanation: The application is vulnerable to clickjacking because it lacks appropriate HTTP headers to prevent it from being embedded in an iframe or frame on a malicious site. This allows an attacker to trick users into performing unintended actions.
ai_advisory.remediation_advice: Implement the X-Frame-Options header with a value of 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN', or use Content-Security-Policy with the 'frame-ancestors' directive to restrict framing.
ai_advisory.risk_summary: Medium. While the target is a local cache endpoint, successful clickjacking could lead to unauthorized actions or session manipulation if the endpoint is used in a sensitive context.
ai_advisory.recommendation:
Modern Web browsers support the Content-Security-Policy and X-Frame-Options HTTP headers. Ensure one of them is set on all web pages returned by your site/app.

If you expect the page to be framed only by pages on your server (e.g. it's part of a FRAMESET) then you'll want to use SAMEORIGIN, otherwise if you never expect the page to be framed, you should use DENY. Alternatively consider implementing Content Security Policy's "frame-ancestors" directive.

ai_advisory.gemma_explanation: The application is vulnerable to clickjacking because it lacks appropriate HTTP headers to prevent it from being embedded in an iframe or frame on a malicious site. This allows an attacker to trick users into performing unintended actions.
ai_advisory.remediation_advice: Implement the X-Frame-Options header with a value of 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN', or use Content-Security-Policy with the 'frame-ancestors' directive to restrict framing.

ai_advisory.recommendation:

verification.evaluation_notes: Endpoint unreachable during verification probe (Probe error: <urlopen error [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it>); remains NEEDS_VERIFICATION.

ai_advisory.gemma_explanation: The Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header prevents a document from being opened in a browsing context that shares the same origin as the parent document. Without it, a malicious site could potentially access sensitive information from your application via the parent's browsing context.
ai_advisory.remediation_advice: Implement the COOP header in your server's response headers, typically setting it to 'same-origin' or 'same-site' to restrict context sharing.
ai_advisory.risk_summary: Medium. While not a direct injection vulnerability, the lack of COOP increases the risk of sensitive data leakage through cross-origin context sharing attacks.
ai_advisory.recommendation:
Ensure that the application/web server sets the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header appropriately, and that it sets the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header to 'same-origin' for documents.

'same-origin-allow-popups' is considered as less secured and should be avoided.

If possible, ensure that the end user uses a standards-compliant and modern web browser that supports the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header (https://caniuse.com/mdn-http_headers_cross-origin-opener-policy).

findings.title: Permissions Policy Header Not Set
findings.description: Permissions Policy Header is an added layer of security that helps to restrict from unauthorized access or usage of browser/client features by web resources. This policy ensures the user privacy by limiting or specifying the features of the browsers can be used by the web resources. Permissions Policy provides a set of standard HTTP headers that allow website owners to limit which features of browsers can be used by the page such as camera, microphone, location, full screen etc.

verification.evaluation_notes: Endpoint unreachable during verification probe (Probe error: <urlopen error [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it>); remains NEEDS_VERIFICATION.

ai_advisory.gemma_explanation: The absence of a Permissions Policy header allows web content to potentially access sensitive browser features like camera, microphone, or geolocation without explicit restriction. This increases the attack surface by permitting unauthorized or excessive use of client-side capabilities.
ai_advisory.remediation_advice: Implement the Permissions-Policy HTTP header to explicitly define which browser features are allowed for the page and its embedded resources. For example, use 'Permissions-Policy: geolocation=(), microphone=()' to disable specific features.
ai_advisory.risk_summary: Medium. While not a direct vulnerability leading to data theft, it exposes the application to potential misuse of client-side APIs, impacting user privacy and security posture.
ai_advisory.recommendation: Ensure that your web server, application server, load balancer, etc. is configured to set the Permissions-Policy header.

findings.description: The Anti-MIME-Sniffing header X-Content-Type-Options was not set to 'nosniff'. This issue still applies to error type pages (401, 403, 500, etc.) as those pages are often still affected by injection issues, in which case there is still concern for browsers sniffing pages away from their actual content type.
